narrative:
The model estimates an 81% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most shaped this outlook were your total years of experience, the other job offers you have received, and the sector you work in. Your relatively short overall experience of 1-5 years, which is common among half the people predicted to stay, still pushed the prediction toward leaving. In contrast, having received other job opportunities strongly increased the likelihood of departure, as external offers often signal that someone is actively considering or being pulled elsewhere. Working in the “other” sector, which is less common among those expected to stay, also nudged the outcome in the leaving direction.

Taken together, these elements outweighed positive signals such as your medical insurance, recognition you receive, and manageable commute. The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether additional responsibilities or clearer growth paths could increase your sense of stability. You may want to reflect on how those external opportunities align with your long-term plans before making any decisions.
